title: Safe Driving Rules
before:
1. Operate all trucks strictly under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on every shared route.
2. Inside the building, drive forklifts at no more than 10 km/h on all travel lanes, cross-aisles and staging approaches.
3. Across the outdoor yard, limit speed to 15 km/h and adjust further for weather, surface conditions and queuing trailers.
4. Within marked pedestrian zones and crossings, slow to 5 km/h, make eye contact where possible and give way to people on foot.
5. On dock ramps and leveller approaches, travel at no more than 5 km/h with the load uphill on gradients and forks kept low.
6. Through the main transport aisles, which are 4.0 m wide, keep to the right, hold the centre clearance and sound the horn before blind junctions.
7. Inside rack storage aisles, which are 3.0 m wide, proceed at walking pace when turning, stacking or passing open pick faces.
8. Around pedestrians, stop completely if the walkway boundary is unclear, wait for the person to clear and then move off smoothly.
9. Wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving, remain seated under the overhead guard and keep hands, feet and hi-vis clothing inside the profile.
10. Respect rated capacity on every lift: counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t for the high bays.
11. Before lifting, confirm the pallet, including its load, weighs at most 800 kg and check the load chart when attachments or high lift heights reduce capacity.
12. When placing pallets to racking, verify each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg in total and never force a pallet that exceeds beam or height clearance.
13. Maintain fork height 100-150 mm above the floor during travel, tilt the mast slightly back and look in the direction of travel at all times.

Carry only stable and evenly distributed loads. Re-wrap or re-stack a leaning pallet before transport and return damaged pallets for repair rather than lifting them high.

Park only in marked positions with forks lowered, controls in neutral and parking brake applied. Switch off the truck, remove the key and never leave a raised load unattended in an aisle.

title: Speed Limits
before:
1. Observe a maximum of 10 km/h for all forklift travel inside the building under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
2. Maintain that indoor limit through every internal area, including receiving, bulk storage, picking, dispatch, cold and value-added zones, without exception for empty travel.
3. Outside the building, drive at no more than 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.
4. Reduce speed progressively when transitioning from the yard through dock openings into internal areas so the 10 km/h indoor limit is already established at the threshold.
5. Slow to 5 km/h in every marked pedestrian zone and at every marked pedestrian crossing under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.
6. Give way to pedestrians at those crossings and proceed only when the route ahead is clear and sightlines are fully confirmed.
7. Apply the same 5 km/h maximum on all dock ramps and leveller approaches, whether travelling laden or unladen.
8. Serving the site are 8 dock doors, with dock doors 1-4 assigned to inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 assigned to outbound dispatch.
9. Approach each of those dock doors at ramp speed, because each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller that creates a gradient, gap and surface change.
10. Inspect the leveller plate position and dock edge before crossing, then cross in a straight line without steering, braking hard or accelerating on the plate itself.
11. Inside Zone A in front of dock doors 1-4, retain the 10 km/h indoor limit and drop further to 5 km/h wherever pedestrian markings, inspection activity or staged inbound pallets narrow the route.
12. Within Zone D in front of dock doors 5-8, combine the indoor and ramp rules: hold 10 km/h on the staging apron, then 5 km/h on every ramp and leveller approach during loading and outbound movements.
13. Treat any obscured corner, rack end, cold-zone doorway or pedestrian walkway intersection as a pedestrian zone: slow to 5 km/h, sound the horn where fitted, and widen the turn only within the marked traffic lane.
14. Adjust below the posted maxima in wet, cold, congested or low-visibility conditions, and stop completely rather than pass where passage width or stability is in doubt.
15. Report missing, faded or damaged speed and pedestrian-zone markings for replacement, and continue to apply the indoor, yard, pedestrian-zone and ramp limits by location even where markings are temporarily unclear.

title: Forklift Operating Rules
before:
1. Operate handling equipment only under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and only within your authorisation. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.

2. Do not drive any powered truck without written authorisation. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

3. Understand the accountability behind this rule. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

4. Know the fleet before you book a truck. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts.

5. Respect rated capacities on every lift. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t.

6. Use the correct truck in the high bays. The fleet has 4 reach trucks for the high bays.

7. Never exceed the rated capacity of the assigned truck. Reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t.

8. Select the right pallet jack for the task and floor. The fleet has 8 electric pallet jacks.

9. Report defects on hand equipment immediately. The site has 12 hand pallet jacks.

10. Complete the documented pre-use check every day. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.

11. Observe the correct order for the daily check. The daily forklift check happens BEFORE first use each day.

12. Do not start the shift on an unchecked truck. Confirm the daily record is signed before switching on.

13. Wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.

14. Limit speed inside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building.

15. Control speed in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

16. Slow to walking pace where pedestrians have priority. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings.

17. Approach level edges at low speed. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

18. Adjust speed further for load, visibility and floor condition. Stop and sound the horn where sight lines are restricted.

19. Park only in designated positions with forks lowered, brake applied and power isolated. Hand over keys only to authorised operators.

title: Pedestrian Walkways and Crossings
before:
1. Walk only inside the segregated pedestrian walkways when moving through the warehouse. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are marked for foot traffic only.

2. Wear a high-visibility vest at all times on the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, including visitors and office staff crossing to the zones.

3. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor and applies on walkways, in aisles and at crossings.

4. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse to every movement on foot between Zone A, Zone B, Zone C and Zone D. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

5. Keep to the walkway side when passing Zone B. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Do not step into rack storage aisles unless your task requires access, and check both directions before entering.

6. Cross main transport aisles only at marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Stop at the marking, establish eye contact with the driver, and wait until the truck has stopped.

7. Expect forklifts to slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Do not cross behind a reversing truck. Continue to watch for a second truck in the adjacent lane.

8. Observe the indoor limit during all crossings. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building. Never assume a driver has seen you, even where the 10 km/h limit applies.

9. Stay clear of dock ramps and leveller approaches unless authorised to work there. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Use only the marked pedestrian route to reach the dock areas.

10. Plan picking movements in Zone C to minimise crossing. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Push pallet jacks within the pick aisle and park them clear of the walkway edge.

11. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation at every interface with pedestrians. Give way to loaded trucks at crossings. Keep hands clear of racking and keep walkways free of pallets, film and strapping.

12. Report blocked walkways, faded markings, damaged barriers or lighting faults to the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Do not move barrier tape or enter a closed walkway until it is released.

title: Yard and Dock Safety
before:

2. Reduce speed to 10 km/h immediately on entering the building enclosure.
3. Slow to 5 km/h through every marked pedestrian zone and crossing on yard routes and dock approaches.
4. Approach all dock ramps and leveller approaches at no more than 5 km/h with the load low and forward visibility maintained.
5. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all yard driving, reversing, parking and coupling manoeuvres without exception.
6. Observe PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse where yard footways meet dock stairs, offices and crossing points.
7. Recognise the building has 8 dock doors, each fitted with its own dock leveller.
8. Direct inbound vehicles only to dock doors 1-4 for receiving.
9. Unload inbound trailers in Zone A, the receiving zone for unloading and goods inspection in front of docks 1-4.
10. Stage outbound trailers only at dock doors 5-8 for dispatch.
11. Hold outbound pallets and staged loads in Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
12. Obtain dispatcher assignment before moving any vehicle to a door.
13. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads.
14. Wait for the dispatcher to assign dock doors and time slots to carriers before admitting vehicles to the gate or apron.
15. Prohibit reversing toward an open dock edge unless guides, mirrors and audible warning devices are in use.
16. Inspect the leveller, dock seal, wheel chocks and trailer bed before placing the first pallet.
17. Confirm the trailer is braked, chocked and supported before driving a forklift onto the bed.
18. Keep forklift forks clear of leveller lips, dock edges and door tracks during alignment.
19. Yield to banksmen and pedestrians at all dock corners, roller doors and yard junctions.
20. Sound the horn before exiting the building into the yard and before entering the building from the yard.
21. Park MHE clear of dock approaches, levellers and emergency routes when not loading.
22. Report faulty levellers, damaged doors, uneven yard surfaces or defective lighting for immediate repair.

title: Forklift Operators
before:
1. Operate counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks for put-away, replenishment, loading and yard movements as directed by the shift supervisor. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Work Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

2. Obtain written authorisation before operating any powered truck. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

3. Complete the documented pre-use check every day before first use of the assigned truck. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day. Report defects immediately and do not use faulty equipment.

4. Drive the fleet within rated capacities and designated areas. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks.

5. Observe posted speed limits at all times. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

6. Wear required personal protection on the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.

7. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse when travelling on main transport aisles, in racking and near walkways. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, and segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Give way to pedestrians at crossings and maintain clear sightlines.

8. Serve all functional zones according to tasking. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.

9. Stage and collect outbound loads only as instructed. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Handle chilled pallets for Zone E under instruction.

10. Respect stacking and racking limits on every lift. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg, and a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg.

11. Follow PR-12 Cold-chain handling for movements in and out of the cold zone. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C, with cold-zone temperature manually verified each shift.

12. Follow PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any cage movement. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time, which holds at most 5 full-weight pallets, and never exceed the authorised balance.
